verdict.rationale: HMRC's GOV.UK pages give founders plain-language, second-person guidance on core tasks. Examples include registering with Companies House and then adding Corporation Tax services, the VAT thresholds and voluntary registration, and signing up for Making Tax Digital, including the agent route. The excerpts show conversational explainers rather than statute text, but they are short fragments, so full sequenced step-by-step walkthroughs are only implied. missing for 10: evidence of complete numbered step-by-step walkthroughs for a founder's task end to end, independent or hands-on corroboration that non-lawyers can follow the guidance, and broader coverage of founder tasks beyond these registration pages.

support.subject: As a founder, the service publishes plain-language, step-by-step guidance for my task — explainers a non-lawyer can follow, not just statute text and form numbers

citations.quote: You’ll need to register your company with Companies House. You’ll get the option to be set up for Corporation Tax at the same time.
you’ll need to add Corporation Tax services to your business tax account. You will then be able to manage your Corporation Tax online.
You can choose to register for VAT if your turnover is less than £90,000 (‘voluntary registration’).
You can sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax before you need to use it to help you get ready.
When you sign yourself up, you can make sure your details are correct from the start by: making sure your income sources are up to date
